messages:
sre-oncall: FYI — planning a controlled maintenance window to tune edge cache eviction throttles in us-west-2 this Sunday 02:00–03:00 UTC. Goal is reduce runaway cache churn and lower token cost during high fanout spikes. 

maria: ack. what's the expected customer impact?

sre-oncall: Expected: brief bump in cold-start P95 for generation API routes that miss cache (~200–400ms additional for affected requests). We'll run a 5% canary, then 25% ramp if metrics look good. No planned downtime; fallback to slower model variants if latency exceeds SLO.

josh: can we do a preflight dry-run against a canary pool first?

sre-oncall: yes — plan:
1) preflight against canary pool (5% traffic) for 15m
2) if ok -> 25% for 20m
3) full rollout to region over 30m with 5m observation windows
Abort criteria: error rate spike >0.5% absolute, or P95 increase >400ms sustained for 10m.

elaine: will update on-call runbook with abort criteria and rollback steps.

sre-oncall: runbook snippet (for reference):
```
# set throttle to new value
kubectl -n inferenceset patch configcache throttle --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"evictionThrottle":0.65}}'
# rollback
kubectl -n inferenceset patch configcache throttle --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"evictionThrottle":0.30}}'
```
Also cache-evict job id: evict-canary-{{ts}} (will post exact job id when scheduled).

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance job created: job_id=evict-2026-03-29-02-00-usw2, canary=5%

maria: I'll wire up dashboards: edge-kvcache-hitrate, gen-api-p95, model-fallback-count. Will set alerts at +2x baseline for p95.

josh: recommend enabling KV prefix warmup on canary to avoid cold jitter. quick command:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api/kv/warmup -d '{"prefix":"/gen-cache/"}'
```

sre-oncall: good call — will include warmup step between canary phases.

product-ops: any customer comms needed?

sre-oncall: not proactively unless >15m visible degradation. we'll post to #status if we hit abort and issue >5m customer-visible errors.

infra-bot: Capacity check: GPU pool us-west-2 has 12% spare headroom — OK for canary.

elaine: who's monitoring the rollback channel during the window?

maria: I'll handle dashboards and PagerDuty watch. Josh can be primary responder for cache logic.

josh: got it. I'll be by keyboard 01:45 UTC.

sre-oncall: Thanks — will send a final reminder 1h before. If anyone wants to opt-out of traffic during the canary (app teams), ping me now.

product-ops: noted, will inform support leads about the watch window.

sre-oncall: closing loop: posting runbook link and the exact job id once deploy-bot confirms. :white_check_mark:
